narrative: Aiden Murphy is a 19-year-old college student with severe persistent asthma diagnosed in early childhood and atopic dermatitis. He has a history of multiple asthma exacerbations requiring oral corticosteroids (most recently in 2024) and one hospitalization for severe asthma in 2018. He has documented aspirin/NSAID hypersensitivity (aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease) which causes bronchospasm, and cat dander which triggers asthma exacerbations. His maintenance regimen includes Budesonide/Formoterol 160/4.5 mcg combination inhaler twice daily, Montelukast 10mg in the evening (with awareness of the black box warning for neuropsychiatric effects), and Albuterol as a rescue inhaler. Recent vitals from March 2026 show blood pressure 118/72, heart rate 76, BMI 21.6, peak expiratory flow 620 L/min, FEV1 at 78% predicted, and oxygen saturation 97%. He has never smoked, does not drink alcohol given his age, swims competitively (chosen for low asthma trigger), and follows a typical college diet.
